therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Opioid receptor agonism for analgesia with peripheral opioid antagonism to reduce constipation
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Pain relief while mitigating opioid-induced constipation
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change in Bowel Function Index (BFI) and Brief Pain Inventory Short Form (BPI-SF) at week 4

results.effect_size: BFI: 48.3 vs 51.2 (oxycodone/naloxone vs oxycodone); BPI-SF: 3.7 vs 3.6
subgroup_findings: Similar pain relief between groups across all BPI-SF measures
Slightly better bowel function with oxycodone/naloxone (lower BFI score)
Similar laxative use between groups by week 4
safety_signals: Various serious adverse events including convulsion, gastroenteritis, intentional overdose in oxycodone group
